title: Every ticket is split into its plan and its log
intention: cairn.tools.base.ticket_log.split runs over every ticket plan under CairnCommons/tickets/ (skipping '_' files and non-.json), every one is left holding only plan_fields with its trail in its .log.jsonl, nothing is lost, and the system reads green afterwards.
why: Akien 2026-10-09, verbatim: "the plan is always the 'current what to do' all questions answered, all intentions clear. the questions and the answering of them is in the ticket log." 2026-10-10 he chose the layout "Flat plan + .log.jsonl (Recommended)": tickets/<id>-<slug>.json IS the plan, rewritten in place with no superseded lines, and tickets/<id>-<slug>.log.jsonl beside it is the append-only log, one JSON object per line. Then: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", all pre-approved through PROVED. Intention: /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md. Measured 2026-10-10 (/home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/measurements/2026-10-10-ticket-field-readers.json): 244 top-level fields over 516 tickets, 166 of them read by no non-proof code, so the trail is mostly fields nobody but a reader-mind opens.
traces_to: Law 5 (every existing ticket becomes a plan with its trail beside it in the log); Law 7 (lossless: the log keeps every value the plan drops).
how: Run once, by hand, from cairn/, after 9df0f230a087, 76da3a283277 and fad76bb5d1f5 are PROVED: (1) snapshot: for every tickets/*.json not starting '_', record sha256 and the parsed doc to a scratch file. (2) for each, cairn.tools.base.ticket_log.split(path, actor='cc', why='plan/log split, task 29569fca68a3'). (3) verify each ticket: plan keys subset of plan_fields; reconstruction (as in 76da3a283277's proof 2) equals the snapshot doc. (4) run the build_inspector and the full proof suite (`cairn test`); run rehearsal.rehearse over every ticket whose cursor is not PROVED/SUPERSEDED/RETIRED/KILLED/ABSORBED/DROPPED and collect log_reach_count. (5) commit commons (plans + logs) in one commit naming this task. Record the counts (tickets split, lines by kind, open tickets rehearsed, total log_reaches and the tickets carrying them) in this task's verdict.
falsifier: Proved by instrument, in this task's verdict: (1) for all 516+ tickets the reconstruction equals the pre-split snapshot (count of mismatches == 0); (2) no plan carries a key outside plan_fields (count 0); (3) build_inspector and `cairn test` are no redder than the pre-split run on the same commit (the set of red names after is a subset of before); (4) the plan-only rehearsal has run over every open ticket and its log_reach counts are recorded. Wrong intent if: a ticket's log_reaches show the plan missing something only its trail settles in a way no decision line could carry (the cut is in the wrong place, stop and raise it on the intention), or a code reader goes red because a field it reads moved (the plan_fields census missed a reader: add the field to plan_fields through 76da3a283277's charter, re-run).
watchme: none, because its result is read once by its own falsifier against the snapshot, and from then on drift is refused at the door by 1fc53d5d96cc and the cast door of 76da3a283277; the intention it serves is /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md

The proof is tickets/29569fca68a3-split.md carrying the measured counts, quorum-sealed (cairn.devices.tester.quorum.seal) with Akien's relayed words 'we preapproved all these things thru PROVED', notary cc; PROVEME names it as proven_by; crossings journal at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code. quorum.seal's falsifier is this ticket's FALSIFIER clauses (1)-(4) verbatim, and its horizon is 'until the piece on disk differs from the fingerprint signed'; the claim is the piece's first line. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The parallel run is xargs -P4 over the open ids, each `bin/cairn rehearse <id>` writing its own output file; a run exiting other than 0 (clean) or 1 (gaps) is rerun once; no other tool is needed. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The counts are the check script's own output: each verb (reconstruct, reds, rehearsals) prints one JSON line (lines_by_kind is the count of log lines the split added per log kind; log_reach_total and tickets_carrying_reaches read each rehearsal record's log_reach_count), and the piece copies the three lines verbatim under one heading each. decisions.text: The check script's verbs: reconstruct — for every tickets/*.json (not '_') at the snapshot, ticket_log.reconstruct(plan at the split commit, the log lines that commit added) equals the snapshot doc, and no plan key lies outside plan_fields; reds — the after sets of inspect() finding identities (method|at) and of proofs `bin/cairn test -q` prints RED or UNRUNNABLE are each subsets of the before sets in measurements/2026-10-10-plan-log-split-reds.json; rehearsals — every ticket open at the snapshot has a rehearsals/<id>-<stamp>.json stamped after the split commit, and its log_reach_count is summed. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The check script's reds verb only reads; it never writes the before set. The before and after sets are written by a separate scratch runner, measure_reds.py before|after, run from cairn/ with PYTHONPATH=.: 'before' runs before the split, 'after' after the split commit, both at the same cairn commit; reds exits 2 while either set is missing. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

A ticket's cursor is the bracketed word in its workflow_and_state string, matched by the regex \[([A-Z]+) (e.g. '... -> [BUILDME:waiting] -> ...' is BUILDME); open means that word is not one of the six terminals. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

`bin/cairn test -q` prints one line per red proof, '  RED    <path>' or '  UNRUNNABLE  <path>', matched by ^\s+(RED|UNRUNNABLE)\s+(\S+); inspect() returns a dict whose 'findings' is a list of dicts carrying 'method' and 'at', and a finding's identity is 'method|at'; plan_fields is the list under that key in tickets/_charter+why.json. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

quorum.seal(artifact_path: str, *, claim: str, signatures: list[dict], notary: str, quorum=1, falsifier: str, horizon: str) takes the piece's PATH, fingerprints its bytes, never modifies it, and writes tickets/validations/29569fca68a3-split.json holding exactly that one validation record (it does not append); falsifier and horizon are plain strings. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

decisions.text: The split renames, never adds a key: a plan left with no 'intention' takes its v1 string 'intent', else its v1 'what', as 'intention' (intent wins when both; the other stays in the log); each rename rides the artifact door with one 'renamed' {from, to} log line, declared in the store charter's log_kinds; 'intent' and 'what' are never added to plan_fields; a plan that keeps an 'intention' is left alone; a non-string 'intent' is never promoted. The rename runs as a second commit whose message starts '29569fca68a3: split'; the check's reconstruct verb proves each split commit as plan at it + the lines it added == plan at its parent, and fails on any plan left with no 'intention'. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

decisions.text: A blank or null 'intention' states nothing and counts as none: the split replaces it by the rename D26 names, and the 'renamed' line keeps the blank as 'was' (declared in the store charter's log_kinds) so reconstruct returns it exactly. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
